critical_code_review_comments: routers/leave.py is tight and idiomatic — clear hierarchy via _approver_ids / _can_approve, never-self-approve guard at line 64, _days() defensive parsing, requester DELETE only on own+pending. Inbox query for super_admin correctly $ne self so OA peer admins don't see their own request as inbox.

Lead conversion is idempotent (lines 280-281) and uses lead.assigned_to_user_id as referrer_user_id — correctly credits the staff who worked the lead. Owner defaults to super_admin so the new inquiry student joins the standard students view.

applications.get_referrer (lines 354-370) gracefully falls back to user lookup with type='staff' when no client matches — supports the new CRM /apply?ref=<staff_user_id> link without breaking the legacy slug/client referral flow.
students/me/referrals endpoint is straightforward; consider adding pagination if a popular staff ever crosses ~500 referrals (currently unbounded find).

Minor: leave_requests collection has no explicit indexes referenced in this router. server.py supposedly adds them — verify {requester_user_id:1, status:1} + {office:1, requester_role:1, status:1} indexes exist for inbox query performance at scale.

Frontend StaffDashboard cleanly composes the 4 stats + 3 quick action tiles + referral link box + leads + students-referred panels. data-testid coverage is complete and matches the request spec exactly.
